source.title: Optimizing Neural Networks with Gradient Lexicase Selection

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. It identifies the work as published at ICLR 2022, despite the ID and venue metadata indicating 2023.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a different training method on image-classification datasets and reports held-out test accuracy; its main results do not test most listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that Adam experiments with tuned learning rates performed significantly worse than SGD, but gives no per-model values or detailed setup for those trials. Main tables compare gradient lexicase with SGD and other selection methods; these results concern generalization but do not map to the listed versions.
record.test_reason: Appendix B reports the authors' own Adam trials: after several learning-rate tuning trials, Adam generalized worse than its SGD counterpart. This bears on V4. The main lexicase-versus-SGD comparisons do not test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors conclude that Gradient Lexicase Selection can improve several architectures' test performance and may fail on extensively optimized architectures. Their representation-diversity evidence is qualitative. Table 1 also contains SVHN declines for SENet18 and EfficientNetB0, so improvement is not universal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an evolutionary training framework combining subset gradient descent and lexicase selection; baseline is momentum-SGD. The Adam comparison is mentioned without detailed results.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by architecture and dataset: MobileNetV2 does not improve on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, and SENet18 and EfficientNetB0 decline on SVHN. Population-size and momentum settings also change test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient Lexicase Selection improves mean test accuracy in most Table 1 comparisons, but lowers it for MobileNetV2 on both CIFAR datasets and for SENet18 and EfficientNetB0 on SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient Lexicase Selection can improve held-out image-classification accuracy over momentum SGD, with architecture- and dataset-dependent exceptions.

record.problems: The core comparison uses three random seeds. The authors do not report statistical tests. SVHN excludes the large extra set and is stated to be non-comparable to other work. The Adam comparison is only summarized qualitatively without per-model results or detailed setup.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2–4 report additional comparisons and ablations (selection methods, population sizes, and momentum options), and Section 5.3 reports representation distributions. They are not extracted because they concern the paper's distinct method and do not map directly to the supplied claim versions; the 60-row limit was not reached.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label performance under the same recipe, and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Training-performance comparisons, language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of examples ranked by label memorization versus equally sized random removals.

missing.what: Add a qualitative V4 result for the authors' Adam trials: learning-rate tuning over several trials still yielded worse generalization than SGD. No numerical accuracy, architecture/dataset breakdown, training-performance comparison, or Adam-specific schedule is supplied.
missing.locator: Appendix B, Implementation Details, first paragraph.

record.verdict_notes: The V4 evidence is a qualitative report of the authors' own experiments, separate from their citations to prior work. Their description of Adam's deficit as significant is unsupported by numerical results or a reported statistical test. The existing rows' baseline and accuracy values match Table 1; their states cannot be interpreted against the supplied versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
The paper reports Adam performed significantly worse than SGD after learning-rate tuning, but supplies no separate accuracy values or details sufficient to extract a comparable row.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
